4.3:
Failed to compile the debug version because of some header errors. But the release version from Godot's website does crash.

I observe the same behavior when calling `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().reimport_files()` from `EditorPlugin` - each time either `Condition "p_I->data != this" is true` error or crash. So simplest reproduction is:

```gdscript
extends EditorPlugin

func _enter_tree():
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.5).timeout # just to exclude chance the problem is caused by some ongoing initialization
	EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().reimport_files(["res://assets/image.png"])
```

No error or crash when making the same call from `EditorScript`. However, `EditorScript` requires manual trigger, which is not great for automation, so the workaround is to call `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().scan()`. Less performant, but does not error or crash.

My use case: automatically changing import type for images in a specific directory. I change importer name in `.import` and want to trigger reimport, exactly like in the `reimport_files()` description:
> Call this if these files or their .import files were directly edited by script or an external program.

Still crashes on 4.7.dev in `SceneTree::process_timers` (when running the MRP)
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ef0163ba9ff3ccd8490608afe5bfb344fdc7397b/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp#L812

I'm not sure if it is related, but I'm investigating a crash in a plugin. It throws a similar error before crashing:
```

   at: erase (./core/templates/list.h:228)
```

I narrowed it down to a subroutine call:
```gdscript
EditorInterface.save_scene() # Confirmed saved
await get_tree().create_timer(REIMPORT_CHECK_DELAY).timeout # Crashes here
print("Checkpoint") # Doesn't print
```

However, if I extend the timer, the error will still show, but it doesn't result in a crash.

This is in 4.7.1, but also has been the case for as far back as 4.4. If it's an unrelated bug, then I can open a new ticket and try to make an MRP.
I think it is the bug. It has something to do with scene tree timers. At least everybody who confirmed this had a timer in their code.
